title: Extensions are sandboxed WebAssembly components, not native shared libraries
scope:
how third-party code is added to a running Novis without rebuilding it — the three tiers,
the `.nvsx` component format and its manifest, the WIT world, how a value crosses the guest
boundary, and the isolation, limits and loading rules a guest runs under. Not in scope: which
subsystem belongs at which tier, which is [0051](0051.md); how a package is
named, resolved and granted, which is [0081](0081.md).
validatedBy:
[`benches/abi-probe`](../../benches/abi-probe/) — `tests/wasm_sandbox.rs` and the
`wasm-probe` cost guards. Originally spike #4, on wasmtime 41 + cranelift 0.128,
`x86_64-pc-windows-msvc`.

summary.headline: Extensions run in a WebAssembly sandbox, never as native libraries
summary.body:
An add-on is a WebAssembly component in a single file; there is no way to load a native shared
library or call into C. The extension never sees the server's memory: values stay on the host
side and it reads them through checked handles, so a buggy or hostile extension spoils one
request and nothing else. Each request gets a fresh copy, under that request's own limits and
permissions. Every call across the boundary has a fixed price, so pieces that need raw speed,
such as database drivers, are built into the binary instead.
